content_blocks.label: lead_paragraph
content_blocks.text: Republican lawmakers in Illinois have proposed raising the state’s minimum wage to $15 per hour, a move that has been met with fierce opposition from small business owners and economists.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_1
content_blocks.text: The proposal, which would take effect over a five-year period, would see the minimum wage increase gradually from its current rate of $9.25 per hour.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_2
content_blocks.text: Supporters argue that a higher minimum wage would boost consumer spending and reduce poverty levels, while opponents warn that it could lead to job losses and higher prices for consumers.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_3
content_blocks.text: ‘Small businesses are already struggling to stay afloat, and this would only make things worse,’ said local shop owner Sarah Johnson. ‘I’m worried about being able to keep my doors open if this passes.’

content_blocks.label: pull_quote
content_blocks.text: ‘Raising the minimum wage is a Band-Aid solution that doesn’t address the root causes of economic inequality.’ – Economist Dr. Emily Davis
